newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria should let foreigners buy land - premier.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria should let foreigners buy land - premier.

text.p: Bulgarian Prime Minister Ivan Kostov urged parliament on Tuesday to remove a constitutional ban on foreign citizens owning land in Bulgaria.
Kostov told a news conference that his ruling Union of Democratic Forces would seek other parliamentary parties' support to amend the constitution.

"This is an issue of global and strategic economic importance...it will create incentives for small and medium business and speed up privatisation...it is an excellent opportunity to stimulate economic revival," Kostov said.

Under the country's post-communist constitution passed in 1991, foreign citizens are not allowed to buy land in Bulgaria. Kostov said the restriction reflected Socialist-era views and the European Union had pressed for the law to be changed.
"I expect that it would boost foreigners' interest in privatisation as they would feel much more confident if they own the land under the enterprise as well," Kostov said.

The Union of Democratic Forces, which won the April general election, holds a majority in parliament but needs other parties' support for changes in the constitution that require a two thirds majority.
